answer: At most 3 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a voyage tag. The bridge cap is checked at intake and quartz publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a swarm in one epoch however much capital it holds, as every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
